thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Production alert — multiple inference pods in `runtimes-prod` are being OOM-killed. Autoscaler is marking nodes NotReady in the same AZ. Paging @sophia (oncall) and @aj (runtime lead).

sophia: seeing 502/503 spikes on /v1/generate and a cascade of pod restarts. CPU on affected pods is pegged at 100% for long stretches before the kubelet kills them.

aj: grabbing logs now. preliminary guess: tokenizer worker threads exploding on large prompt batches. posting `kubectl describe` and `journalctl` snippets.

aj: ```
kubectl get pods -n runtimes-prod -o wide | grep tokenize
runtoken-7d9c8   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5   10m   10.0.4.22   ip-10-0-3-45
runtoken-9a2b1   1/1     Running            0   8m    10.0.4.23   ip-10-0-3-46
```

aj: ```
# from pod logs (tokenizer container)
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] WARN Prompt length 1.2M chars — starting chunking
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] ERROR CPU usage 99.9% - memory alloc fail
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 32456 (tokenizer) score 987
```

sophia: confirm customers seeing failures: error rate for text-generation up from 0.6% -> 9.8% in last 5m. Top affected routes are batch/generate and streaming with very long system prompts.

maria: tagging infra — looks like several nodes reported kubelet evictions around same time. Could be a hotspot on tokenizer path that's single-threaded and uses huge temporary buffers.

aj: quick mitigation options I can do now: 1) add a short-term admission control to reject requests with prompt_size > 500k chars, 2) scale tokenizer deployment to additional nodes (if we have spare capacity), 3) restart the evicted pods after lowering concurrency env var. Prefer 1+3 immediately.

kate: +1 for prompt-size gate. We need to avoid restarting in tight loop — set backoff. Also, can we push a temp nginx filter at the edge to reject/return 413 for oversized requests?

opsbot: Deploy plan started by @aj: create feature-flagged limiter on tokenizer service, will rollout canary to 2 pods. CI/CD job kicked: CD-2458.

aj: applying a runtime env change to limit TOKENIZER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 and PROMPT_MAX_CHARS=500000 on the canary. Command: ```
kubectl set env deployment/tokenizer -n runtimes-prod TOKENIZER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 PROMPT_MAX_CHARS=500000 --record
```

sophia: doing customer triage — which customers impacted? Dashboards show 3 big customers with sustained errors: acme-analytics, docflow-ai, and research-labs. Notifying CSMs and starting a private incident channel.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: @sophia to @maria in 25m. Please document actions and open a postmortem ticket.

aj: canary rolled out. Observing logs: canary pods processed large prompts with chunking now and CPU stabilized around 40-60%. Old pods still OOM-killed during restart attempts.

aj: snippet from canary logs: ```
[INFO] prompt_size=820000 -> rejected by PROMPT_MAX_CHARS, returning 413
[INFO] chunked request into 3 segments, tokenizer queue length 2
```

maria: taking over oncall. thanks @sophia. Latest state: 2 canary pods healthy, 4 old pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Cluster has 12 nodes; 2 nodes marked NotReady due to kubelet memory pressure.

maria: immediate next steps I'm pushing: 1) cordon the two pressure nodes to avoid scheduling, 2) trigger node drain + restart for them, 3) increase HPA min replicas for tokenizer to 6 with PodDisruptionBudget, 4) leave prompt gate in place for 1 hour and monitor.

kate: communicating externally: CSMs drafted customer note — impacted requests may have seen 5-15% elevated errors during 14:00-14:45 UTC, primarily for very large prompts. Recommend telling customers to trim system prompts and use streaming with smaller chunks for now.

opsbot: k8s actions executed: cordon ip-10-0-3-45, drain started, restart node requested. HPA update applied.

aj: monitoring metrics: CPU tail latency down, error rate dropped to 1.2% after gate + canary. No CUDA errors observed — this looks purely CPU/oom on tokenizer process.

sophia: confirmed customer impact window and list. Opening incident ticket INC-2026-0315 and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem.

maria: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis: unbounded prompt sizes cause tokenizer to allocate O(N) temporary buffers on CPU, and certain request patterns (single large batch of long prompts) serialized onto one worker thread causing memory blowout. Secondary contributor: lack of an early admission control and conservative resource limits on tokenizer container.

aj: long-term fixes I propose: - enforce prompt size and tokenization timeouts at edge, - incremental tokenization with streaming to avoid huge intermediate allocations, - set resource requests/limits higher for tokenizer or split into a separate service for large prompt handling, - add unit and load tests for extreme prompt cases.

maria: for immediate follow-ups: create runbook for tokenizer OOM: default PROMPT_MAX_CHARS=500k, TOKENIZER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8, alert when pod OOM rate > 1/min, and automated rate-limiter at ingress.

sophia: handoff complete to @maria — I'm stepping off. Thanks team. (reacted with :thumbsup:)

maria: I'll keep the incident channel updated as nodes come back. Tentative timeline: nodes restarted and cluster stable by +40m, follow-up postmortem in 48h.

opsbot: Node ip-10-0-3-45 restarted at 2026-03-15T15:05:02Z. All tokenizer pods eventually recovered after gating and restart sequence.

kate: CSM updates sent. Customers on the impacted list offered 1 week of free credits for disruptions.

maria: closing notes: mitigations worked — gate + canary + node restart. Postmortem ticket INC-2026-0315 contains action items. Will schedule a workshop to design streaming tokenizer changes.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring.
